Drumming Up a World of Sound
In the 1980s, Evelyn Glennie attended London’s
Royal Academy of Music. In retrospect, her
professors cautioned her that no one had
solo percussionist. Unwilling to accept this advice,
Glennie proceeded to put solo percussion on the map.
Little had been written for the genre, so Glennie
composed or commissioned hundreds of pieces,
captivating audiences with her innovative musicianship.
She also earned acclaim through an array of collaborations
with groups ranging from symphonies to rock bands.
Whether in a classroom or a concert hall, Glennie
always performs barefoot. Having lost nearly all hearing
ability as a child, she realized at the age of twelve—when
she began studying percussion—that she could listen with
more than her ears. Having bare feet helps her feel
vibrations and detect certain pitches by using her feet
Feeling sound throughout her body has given
Glennie insight as a composer. She listens quite intensely
to the clatter of a city street as she does to the harmonies
of an orchestra, internalizing experiences that enrich her
